create.sourceHint: Link up to {max} tasks. The selected tasks' persistent blackboard, asset scope, and related traffic are inherited as read-only. The new task writes to its own independent blackboard.
create.companyHint: Assets from the selected company are added to "Test Assets" and domains/IPs/CIDRs/ICPs/keywords are provided to the agent as scope context. Does not auto-generate intents or force execution goals.
create.interceptHint: Applies to this task only, not global rules. Evaluation: first check block rules (including global), if matched, testing is denied. If not matched and this task has allow rules, the request must match at least one allow rule; otherwise testing is also denied. If no allow rules are set, no whitelist is applied.
create.llmHint: Failover in listed order. First item is current config; only switches to next when quota is depleted.
create.timeoutPlaceholder: Leave empty for no time limit
create.timeoutHint: When the time is reached, a graceful shutdown is executed (each agent writes results + planner makes final judgment), and the task enters timeout-ended state.
create.heartbeatHint: If this duration passes since the last planning cycle or task start with no triggers, a planning cycle is automatically run (prevents stalls + resumes worker supervision). Minimum 10 minutes.
create.seedHint: When enabled, immediately delivers description+goals as a single intent so the worker starts without waiting for the first planning cycle. The planner takes over when done to evaluate and supplement. Recommended for CTF-like scenarios that can usually be solved in one run. Disabled means standard: plan first, then execute.
create.coverageHint: Default is on. Calculates and shows test coverage, shows test progress in the map, and auto-accumulates test scope. When off, coverage is no longer calculated/shown, the map shows assets only without progress, and agents no longer receive scope-related tools. Turning off does not affect "Related company asset scope".

trafficCapture.title: Traffic Capture
trafficCapture.desc:
When on, all HTTP traffic from agents passes through a recording proxy and is fully saved. Agents receive traffic_search/traffic_get tools and proxy settings (proxy description included in prompt).

When off (default), no traffic is recorded. Agents do not receive proxy settings or traffic tools, and the prompt contains no proxy-related content. Toggling immediately re-creates agents.
trafficCapture.on: On · Recording traffic and injecting proxy
trafficCapture.off: Off · No recording or proxy injection

agentBinding.title: Agent Auto Traffic Binding
agentBinding.desc:
Default is off. When on, a report agent running when a finding is recorded cross-references existing HTTP requests/responses and links matching traffic before writing the report. Querying packets and making extra tool calls increases token consumption.

Can still report normally when TCP-only, no packets captured, or no matching traffic. This switch does not affect traffic capture, manual binding, or viewing saved evidence. Applies from the next agent run; turning off immediately rejects new auto-bindings.

globalProxy.title: Global Proxy
globalProxy.desc:
All agent outbound traffic routes through this proxy (hide source IP / use relay server). Supports http / https / socks5 with optional user:pass auth. Empty means direct connection.

When Traffic Capture is on, this proxy becomes the upstream of the recording proxy. When off, it is injected directly into agent bash/WebFetch output. Independent of web search proxy and LLM proxy.
globalProxy.configured: Configured · All outbound traffic through this proxy
globalProxy.notConfigured: Not configured · Outbound traffic via direct connection

constraints.title: Action Constraint Injection
constraints.desc:
When on, each task's action constraints (allow/deny items managed in task overview "Action Constraints") are appended to the agent's system prompt to scope exploration (e.g. "test current ports only", "no brute force").

Can control injection for planner and worker independently. Default is both on. Toggles take effect immediately (read on next cycle) without re-creating agents. Turning off means the agent no longer sees constraints.

experimental.title: Experimental Features
experimental.desc:
Features still under validation; default is off. May change agent behavior or affect stability. Understand the impact before enabling.

noa context compression: Model directly compresses long conversation history (norma v0.4.0). When on, the four agent types connected to the platform (planner / worker / main agent / conversation) use noa instead of built-in compression; compressed originals are kept in the task directory for review. Toggles take effect immediately without re-creating agents. Turning off immediately reverts to built-in compression.

webSearch.title: Web Search
webSearch.desc:
Web search master switch + source configuration. Must be on to individually enable web_search in each agent config (returns title/link/summary only; full content is fetched by WebFetch). Web search does not go through the recording proxy and is independent of traffic capture.

Sources: DuckDuckGo (ddgs) (no key needed), Brave (free tier) (Brave API Key required), Tavily (Tavily API Key required), DeepSeek (reuses current LLM config).
webSearch.on: Master switch on · Can be individually enabled in each agent config
webSearch.off: Off · Web search cannot be enabled for any agent
webSearch.deepseekDesc1: This source reuses the currently active LLM config as-is. It therefore only supports official DeepSeek models and the config must use the anthropic protocol. DeepSeek's OpenAI protocol endpoint does not support server-side search. Changing LLM config may break this source.
webSearch.deepseekDesc2: Unlike other sources, search is executed by DeepSeek's server. Each search consumes an extra model call (token cost). Search requests do not go through the exit proxy above and are not included in traffic records. Results contain title and link only (no summary); WebFetch fetches full content.
webSearch.deepseekDesc3: You must verify the above conditions yourself; the system does not block. Use the "Search Test" button below to do a live check.
webSearch.braveNeedsKey: Brave selected but no key set yet. Search tool will not activate until the key is saved.
webSearch.braveQuota: Free tier allows ~2,000 searches/month. Get a key at https://brave.com/search/api/
webSearch.tavilyNeedsKey: Tavily selected but no key set yet. Search tool will not activate until the key is saved.
webSearch.tavilyGetKey: Sign up and get your API key at https://tavily.com
webSearch.proxyHint: Independent exit proxy for search endpoint access only (VPN/SOCKS etc.). Unrelated to MITM recording proxy. Used when network access is blocked.
webSearch.testHint: Actually searches for "test" with current config (source + proxy + key) to verify it works.

pool.title: LLM Pool · Failover
pool.desc: When on, agents without a specified model automatically switch to the next config when the current one is unavailable (insufficient balance / expired key / rate limit / service error).

enable.label: Use pool
enable.hint: Default is off. When off, always uses the active config; fails immediately on error.

bindFallback.label: Fallback even when model is specified
bindFallback.hint: Default is off: if an agent or task specifies a config, only that config is used; fails immediately on error (no silent model switching). When on, specified config failures fall back to the pool chain below.

order.label: Pool order
order.tooFew: Only {n} config(s) available; pool cannot function. Need at least 2 configs with API keys participating in the pool.

recoverNow.title: Recover now: clear circuit trip and retry this config on next call

pool.note: Active config is always priority 1; others are ordered by priority (configured per card). When a config fails, it enters cooldown (60s→35min); skipped during cooldown, auto-reincluded on recovery. Configs that can't fit the current request in context window are skipped. Agents and tasks with a specified model don't participate in the pool by default.

profile.descNew: Creating does not auto-activate. Click "Set active" on the card to use it.
profile.descEdit: Edit then click save. Active config changes take effect immediately for all agents.

thinkingType.label: Thinking switch · thinking.type
thinkingType.hint: Controls whether to send the thinking field. Don't send = omit this field (compatible with models that don't support it like MiniMax); Off = send disabled; On = send enabled. Independent of the intensity below.

effort.label: Thinking effort · reasoning_effort
effort.hint: Independent effort level (OpenAI reasoning_effort / Anthropic output_config.effort). Some interfaces have no thinking field and can enable thinking with effort alone, so effort can be set separately without sending the thinking switch.

toast.nameModelRequired: Please enter a name and model
toast.created: Created: {name} (click "Set active" on the card to use it)
toast.savedActive: Saved. Active config takes effect immediately; no restart required

proxy.label: Proxy (optional)
proxy.hint: Only LLM outbound requests go through this proxy. Supports http/https/socks5, can include credentials (e.g. socks5://user:pass@host:port, URL-encode special chars in password). Leave empty for no proxy (direct connection).

sessionHeader.label: Custom Session Header (optional)
sessionHeader.hint: When filled, this HTTP header is sent with every request, and the header value is automatically set to the current session's session ID (e.g. conv-12 for chat sessions, exp3-worker-i87 for workers). For gateways using session-id headers for prompt caching/sticky routing. Stable within the same session across multiple turns, different between sessions. Leave empty to skip.

profile.rateHint: Rate limit 0 = unlimited, shared across all agents. Context window unit is K (thousands of tokens), 0 = default 200K, max 1000 (i.e. 1M). Setting too high prevents compression from triggering.

priority.label: Pool priority
priority.hint: Higher numbers are selected first. The active config always has first priority regardless of this value. Configs with equal priority take turns, naturally distributing quota.

exclude.label: Exclude from pool
exclude.hint: When enabled, this config won't be used for fallback (still usable if explicitly specified by an agent or task). Useful for expensive configs dedicated to specific agents that shouldn't be consumed when others fail.

streaming.label: Streaming output · streaming
streaming.hint: When enabled (default), operates via streaming SSE for real-time progress and live token counts. When disabled, operates as true non-streaming (stream:false, returns complete response at once) — can bypass some gateway SSE issues (empty frames/missing thinking frames) but loses real-time progress.

maxTokens.label: Output limit · max tokens
maxTokens.hint: Maximum tokens to generate in a single response, sent with every request. 0 (default) = don't send this field, use server default. Different from 'Context window' above which is the total model capacity used only for local compression threshold calculation. Setting too low may cause reasoning models to be cut off mid-thought and produce no output.

maxTokensFieldHint.openai: Specifies which key to send the limit as. max_tokens is the default and most compatible gateways only recognize this. However, official OpenAI reasoning models (o-series/GPT-5) only recognize max_completion_tokens and will return an unsupported_parameter error if max_tokens is sent.
maxTokensFieldHint.anthropic: Only selectable in OpenAI format. Anthropic's field name is fixed as max_tokens.
maxTokensFieldHint.openai-responses: Only selectable in OpenAI format. Responses API field name is fixed as max_output_tokens.

budgetTokens.label: Thinking budget · budget_tokens
budgetTokens.hint: Sets thinking.budget_tokens for Anthropic extended thinking. 0 = don't send (default).

connect.title: Connection retry
connect.trigger: No connection or 200 not yet received: connection reset / read-write timeout / DNS failure and other network-layer errors, plus HTTP 408·429·500·502·503·504.
connect.skips: Other status codes (400/401/403/404/413/422 etc.) are definitive rejections that would fail again on retry, so they're passed up immediately.
connect.desc: Re-sends the same request. Once the stream has started (200 already received), mid-stream disconnects are not handled here.
connect.offHint: -1 = never retry, immediately pass failure up

empty.title: Empty response retry
empty.trigger: HTTP 200 with normal stop finish_reason but no content blocks in the entire response. Gateway empty frames, missing thinking frames, and sampling hiccups all appear this way.
empty.skips: Excludes cases where content is absent due to max_tokens truncation (that needs a higher output limit; retrying hits the same wall).
empty.desc: Re-sends the full prompt; expensive in long contexts, so don't set the count too high.

stream.title: Same-provider safe-window retry
stream.trigger: Issues after stream is established (200 received): mid-stream disconnect, provider overloaded, 429/5xx error events inside the stream, and no tokens have been forwarded to the caller yet.
stream.skips: Quota exhausted (402/insufficient_quota, handled by pool config switch), context overflow (413/context length, handled by compression), 400/401/403/404/422 definitive rejections are not retried.
stream.desc: Replays the same request with the same config. Since no output has been forwarded yet, replaying doesn't duplicate model output or tool execution.
stream.offHint: -1 = on stream disconnect, immediately hand off to outer intent re-run

breaker.title: Pool circuit breaker
breaker.trigger: Trips when temporary failures (429·5xx·network) accumulate consecutively to the threshold. Definitive failures (402 insufficient balance, 401/403 key expired, 404 model not found) trip the breaker immediately without counting.
breaker.skips: Resets to 0 on a single success, so an occasionally flaky config doesn't slowly accumulate to a trip.
breaker.desc: Tripped config enters cooldown; pool skips it during cooldown. Auto-reincluded on recovery. State is persisted to DB and survives restarts.
breaker.attemptsLabel: Trip after how many consecutive failures
breaker.offHint: -1 = never trip on temporary failures (definitive failures still trip)

intent.title: Intent re-run
intent.trigger: Cases not caught by earlier layers: worker ends with model_error. Inner retries exhausted, or stream disconnect after output was already being forwarded (replay would be unsafe; must re-run the whole intent).
intent.skips: Quota exhaustion is already handled by pool config switching, so no re-run here. Task paused/ended/wrapping up yields immediately and doesn't consume backoff time.
intent.desc: Re-runs the full intent from scratch. The outermost layer; each re-run multiplies the inner layers' counts again.
intent.offHint: -1 = no re-run, immediately mark the intent as blocked

override.label: Retry override
override.hint: Applies to this config only, overriding the global defaults on the Retry & Backoff page. Leave each field empty to follow global. Set count to -1 to disable retries for this layer. Fill interval to use fixed interval instead of exponential backoff. Circuit breaker and intent re-run are per-process and can only be adjusted on the global page.

retry.intro: A single model call failure passes through five retry layers in order from inner to outer: <chain>connection → empty response → same-provider safe-window → pool circuit breaker → intent re-run</chain>. Inner layers must be exhausted before the outer layer takes over, so counts <emph>multiply</emph>. Maxing out all layers can burn dozens of requests from a single hiccup. Leave all empty for current defaults, identical to behavior before this page existed. The first three layers can be overridden per model config.

headers.label: Custom request headers
headers.help: One KEY=VALUE per line. e.g. Authorization=Bearer xxx

body_template.label: Request body template
body_template.help: Leave empty for built-in default. Variables: '{{.Title}} {{.Batch}} {{.Count}} {{.HomeURL}} {{.SentAt}}' and under range .Items: .Name/.VulnClass/.Severity/.Summary/.Assets/.DetailURL/.StatusLabel. tls.label: Implicit TLS
